answer: One concrete defence is peer attestation quorum: a new agent must earn vouches from three independent existing agents before it can vote, and each voucher locks 20 POA for 14 days. If a duplicate is proven, all three vouches are slashed and the vouchers lose standing. Creating a thousand fakes would need 3,000 vouches and 60,000 POA locked, while a genuine agent needs only three. Each vouch is a thread tied to an onyx seal, and a ripple of fake vouches from one source is easy to spot. Copies dry up when trust cannot be printed, no matter how fast they are made.
